messages:
ashley: PagerDuty alert fired — multiple Dedicated GPU hosts in us-central1 showing PCIe AER / ECC warnings and kernel-initiated reboots. Seeing increased 502s & timeouts on cs-embed-prod. Paging oncall.

oncall-bot: @mike is on-call (primary). Incident channel created. Severity: P1. PD incident: RDW-4921.

mike: I'm on it, responding to PD. Can someone paste the affected host list? I'll start collecting serial logs and kernel oops.

ashley: infra-bot already pulled a first-pass list: gpu-us-central-12, gpu-us-central-14, gpu-us-central-21. All are Dedicated GPU hosts on GCP N2d+A100. I saw AER errors followed by watchdog/kexec reboots on two nodes. Customer impact: embedding requests slowed, some 502 spikes.

infra-bot: Affected instances: [gpu-us-central-12, gpu-us-central-14, gpu-us-central-21]. Detected events: pci aerr, ecc multi-bit, kernel panic, instance reboot. Logs archived to gs://redwood-incidents/RDW-4921/*.

katie: Handoff: i can take incident for mitigation if mike wants to focus on RCA. mike: do you want me to coordinate migrations and cordon nodes?

mike: Yes pls. katie take mitigation. I'll do logs & timeline. jgonzalez please help with hypothesis and GCP support.

jgonzalez: grabbing dmesg from gpu-us-central-12 now. Snippet below: 
```
[    5.123456] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: ID 0000
[    5.123466] nvidia: Corrected ECC memory error detected
[    5.234567] kernel: NMI: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 22s
[   65.987654] Kernel panic - not syncing: watchdog: hung tasks
-- Reboot --
```

jgonzalez: That looks like corrected ECC then soft lockup then panic. Could be driver/hardware interaction or noisy neighbor triggering PCIe errors.

ashley: Timeline (collected so far):
- 13:02 UTC: alert threshold crossed — 502 rate up 4x for cs-embed-prod.
- 13:04 UTC: gpu-us-central-12 logged first AER/ECC corrections.
- 13:07 UTC: gpu-us-central-12 kernel panic & reboot.
- 13:10 UTC: traffic autoscaled & routed off the host; some requests still saw 502 on upstream LB.
- 13:16 UTC: gpu-us-central-14 logged similar AER/ECC then reboot.
- 13:22 UTC: gpu-us-central-21 logged repeated AER messages but has not yet rebooted.

mike: collecting serial console from all three. Running: `gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output gpu-us-central-12 --zone=us-central1-c` and `journalctl -k -b -1 --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'` to scrape.

katie: mitigation actions in progress:
- cordoned gpu-us-central-21, drained pods, launched fallback pool nodes in us-west1.
- toggled Dedicated autoscale to avoid placing new workloads on affected hosts.
- customer communication: sent triage note to affected accounts A+B with ETA of 60m.

ashley: Customer impact: approximately 12% of embedding traffic hit Dedicated pool in us-central1 during the window; ~2 customers reported increased latency and transient 502s. No data loss reported.

jgonzalez: hypotheses (tracked here so we don't lose them):
1) Noisy neighbor (co-located VM exhausting PCIe bus bandwidth or resetting device) causing AER then kernel panic.
2) Host firmware or BIOS regression on the host image that causes PCIe controller to behave poorly under load.
3) GPU driver/kernel combo regression interacting poorly with ECC corrections (multi-bit) resulting in panic.
4) Underlying GCP hardware/firmware issue (we should correlate with GCP host events).

mike: Evidence so far: ECC entries are present; some are single-bit corrected, then multi-bit; followed by soft lockups. That leans toward hardware or driver rather than purely noisy neighbor, but noisy neighbor could trigger errors. Need GCP host logs and maintenance events. I've opened a GCP support case (case: 1409123). Linking logs and instance serial outputs to case.

gcp-status-bot: GCP: no active region-wide maintenance posted for us-central1 at this time.

ashley: Can we confirm host firmware/BIOS levels? infra-bot: list image/firmware for those instances.

infra-bot: gpu-us-central-12: host firmware v4.2.1, GPU driver 525.60, kernel 6.1. gpu-us-central-14: firmware v4.2.1, driver 525.60, kernel 6.1. gpu-us-central-21: firmware v4.1.9, driver 525.60, kernel 6.1.

jgonzalez: interesting: gpu-us-central-21 is on older firmware. Might point to firmware regression in 4.2.1, but 21 hasn't rebooted yet despite being older. Need to check error rates per host and any colocated instance activity.

mike: pulled top output from before panic on node-12: `kworker` and `ksoftirqd` were busy, I/O wait spiked. Also saw a co-located host with heavy PCIe DMA from a video-encoding VM — possible noisy neighbor.

katie: For immediate mitigation, i've: cordoned remaining Dedicated gpu hosts in the zone, forced reschedule of pods to other regions, and increased capacity in us-west1. Also disabled burst placements for Dedicated pools in us-central1.

ashley: Action items (live):
- katie: finish draining gpu-us-central-21 and keep it cordoned until further notice. (in progress)
- mike: attach serial logs & dmesg to PD & GCP case. (in progress)
- jgonzalez: correlate host firmware + maintenance events + noisy neighbor telemetry. (in progress)
- infra: consider kernel downgrade to 5.15 candidate on a canary host if we can reproduce safely. (blocked until we have repro)

mike: PD and GCP case updated with logs/SER. GCP engineer assigned; they asked for additional lspci and `lspci -vvv` output and host serial logs. I've uploaded to gs://redwood-incidents/RDW-4921/attachments/.

jgonzalez: quick repro attempt on a spare host: running synthetic PCIe stress util (pci-stress) + memtest on GPU — after 20m we saw increased corrected ECC counts on the GPU and sporadic AER messages. Not a full panic, but raises probability of noisy neighbor triggering hardware-level errors.

katie: Customer comms: sent followup note that we mitigated by draining affected hosts, rolling traffic, and are working with GCP to root cause. Next update in 45m or on resolution.

ashley: Note for RCA: collect per-host PCIe AER counters, ECC correction counts, host CPU & I/O usage, list of co-located VMs and their activity, kernel oops stacks, and firmware revision mapping. We'll also link to GCP case.

mike: Short-term conclusion: avoid scheduling Dedicated GPU on these affected racks and coordinate with GCP. Medium-term: consider isolating GPU hosts further (no general-purpose VMs co-located) or require host-scheduling constraints.

jgonzalez: Adding hypothesis priority: 1) firmware/driver interplay, 2) noisy neighbor triggering latent hardware faults, 3) pure GCP hardware failure. We'll update as we get more from GCP.

oncall-bot: Incident RDW-4921 status: mitigation in place, pages suppressed, response team engaged.

ashley: Thanks all — i'll consolidate timeline + artifacts into the incident doc after we close. If anyone sees additional reboots, ping here and re-open PD.

mike: Closing oncall tasks for now, continuing to monitor logs.

katie: gpu-us-central-21 fully drained and cordoned. No further reboots in last 12m. Keeping cordon for minimum 2h.

jgonzalez: GCP engineer replied: they see AER logged at hypervisor and host level; they're running deeper diagnostics and will check for host firmware rollback possibility. They requested we keep afflicted instances cordoned.

ashley: OK. We'll await GCP findings. Notes saved to gs://redwood-incidents/RDW-4921/ and incident doc RDW-4921-draft.md.

mike: I'm going offline to sleep (night shift). If anything critical, PD will escalate. Good handover. :thumbsup:

ashley: good handoff, thanks everyone.
